key_insight: A structured, ten-step LLM-assisted workflow can support complete machine-checked verification of complex algorithms in Dafny while preserving human oversight.
engineering_relevance: The approach could shift verification effort from detailed proof construction toward specification review, solver diagnosis, and strategic guidance.
method: Formalize algorithms and develop contracts and invariants.
Empirically test invariants and iteratively construct proofs using testing and verification feedback.
Profile verification bottlenecks and optimize proofs under resource constraints.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluated the workflow on 37 graph-theory and labelled-transition-system algorithms, including the Hopcroft–Tarjan triconnectivity test, with many verifications completed within hours to a few days.
watch_item: Human review remains essential: machine-checked proofs establish compliance with formal specifications, not whether those specifications capture the intended requirements.
